original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: For one zero-frame word on arbitrary dirty x, two helpers and three targets, prove semantic H2/K boundary equality for the helper-star wrap and price the first q at which it saves scalar ADDs over the matching direct word.
scope_change_reason: The broad H2-sem contract and source-bound R439 helper wraps already have prior artifacts (PR1194, PR1782/1805/1937/2033). Final live overlap also found open PR #3533 (head c61d746404e534affd9fbcba1f2e448e45c06e42) auditing a single restored edge against the literal K mask, and open PR #2721 (head 6b14e212a1aba401d29f2bf7378e745ee2aed7f2) on framed necessity of the no-target-feedback clause. This result avoids both source-bound questions: it narrows to the first profitable abstract three-target word, keeps no-target-feedback, and gives its complete local invoice.
bottleneck_link: A replacement interface is useful only if a positive legal word preserves the arbitrary-dirty boundary and its full local bill is favorable; this microinstance checks the first break-even without claiming supplier-level moment improvement.
stop_rule: Stop after the smallest positive q is derived and the q=3 word passes its exact 64-state boundary, both chronological directions, semantic K equality, and complete local ADD/F/B invoice. Stop earlier on any counterexample; do not extend to an R439 construction search.
evidence: The first-step R439 orientation verifier passes at the assigned base. The new q=3 word passes all 64 binary dirty states in both directions, has exact N=K, uses 5 rather than 6 scalar ADDs, and has F=B=3 against F=B=3 for the direct word. Two malformed controls fail. Final live overlap: PR #3533 head c61d746404e534affd9fbcba1f2e448e45c06e42 and PR #2721 head 6b14e212a1aba401d29f2bf7378e745ee2aed7f2; neither source-bound object is reused.
